Stop reading walls of AI text: Karpathy's four-step ladder

Simplified English, diagrams, HTML pages and custom videos. Choose the format before you ask the question.

verified★★★★★ Based on felixreedai (@felixreedai) · full analysis

Most of us still use chatbots the way we used search engines: ask a question, scroll through a wall of prose, skim, forget. Andrej Karpathy, who now works on pretraining at Anthropic, has suggested a better habit. Treat the answer's format as part of the prompt.

His ladder has four rungs. First, ask for answers in ASD-STE100, the controlled "Simplified Technical English" written for aircraft maintenance manuals: short sentences, plain words, one idea per line. His tip is to follow it only about 80% of the way, so the text stays clear without sounding robotic. Second, ask for a diagram whenever the idea has structure. Third, ask for a small HTML page when you want to play with the idea, such as a calculator with sliders instead of a paragraph about compound interest. Fourth, ask for a bespoke explainer video, which is the format he's most excited about.

The idea behind it: code and model output are now cheap enough that a custom, single-use artifact made just for you is often the best answer to a question.

Try this
  • Next time you ask Claude to explain something, add "answer in ASD-STE100, about 80% strict" and compare the result with your usual answer.
  • For any process or system, ask for a diagram (Mermaid or SVG) before you ask for prose.
  • Turn one money or design question into a one-file HTML page with sliders, and keep it as a tool.
Pay attention to
  • Explainer videos with narration need a text-to-speech service such as ElevenLabs, or a local TTS model.
  • A diagram can look authoritative and still be wrong. Check its labels against the source.
Links
  • ASD-STE100: https://www.asd-ste100.org (unverified)
  • Summary of the four rungs: https://justbeingresourceful.com/2026/10/19/andrej-karpathys-4-rung-ladder-for-understanding-ai-output-asd-ste100-diagrams-html-video/

p5.brush puts pencil, charcoal and watercolour into your code

An MIT-licensed library that makes generative work look drawn by hand.

verified★★★★★ Based on index.opensource (@index.opensource) · full analysis

Generative art often gives itself away with perfect vector lines. p5.brush, by Alejandro Campos Uribe, is a p5.js library that removes that look on purpose. It builds each stroke by stamping a brush tip repeatedly along a path, and varies the spacing, scatter and pressure, the way a real pencil or marker behaves.

It comes with eleven brushes, from graphite grades and a rotring pen to markers, spray and charcoal. Vector fields bend lines as if a hand were following a current. The watercolour fills follow Tyler Hobbs' published layering method, and where colours overlap they're mixed with spectral.js, so blue and yellow really do make green instead of a muddy grey. Hatching fills shapes with drawn lines.

For anyone working on prints, posters or generative visuals, it's a quick way to get a hand-made look without leaving code. Because it's MIT-licensed, you can use it in commercial work.

Try this
  • Port a sketch you already have to p5.brush and swap the line() calls for brush strokes.
  • Make a print series where only the vector-field seed changes from piece to piece.
  • Test the spectral mixing: overlap two watercolour fills and compare the result with normal alpha blending.
Pay attention to
  • Natural-media rendering is heavier than plain vectors, so render high-resolution stills offline instead of in real time.
  • Spectral mixing changes colours on purpose. Proof your palette before you print.
Links
  • p5.brush: https://github.com/acamposuribe/p5.brush
  • p5.js: https://p5js.org

Before Primetime: catch up on Lance Oppenheim

Lance Oppenheim has two of autumn's most talked-about films, so here's the back catalogue to watch first.

verified★★★☆☆ Based on Christie Boschman (@thatdocumentarygirl) · full analysis

Lance Oppenheim has had quite an October. Primetime, his first scripted feature, stars Robert Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen and is produced for A24. You Can See Everything, made with Nathan Fielder, follows Elizabeth Holmes around the time she reported to prison. It premiered at a secret Telluride screening where audience phones were taken away, and it opened in US cinemas on October 16.

Documentary recommender Christie Boschman makes the case for going back to his earlier work, and every title checks out. Some Kind of Heaven (2020) is a dreamlike portrait of The Villages in Florida, America's largest retirement community. Spermworld (FX) follows people who arrange sperm donation through Facebook groups instead of clinics. Ren Faire, a three-part HBO series from 2024, turns the succession fight at the Texas Renaissance Festival into something close to Succession in chainmail.

What ties them together is a stylised, almost fictional look at real and often odd American subcultures. That's why a jump to a scripted, true-story-based film like Primetime makes sense.

Try this
  • Start with Some Kind of Heaven. It's short, and it's the clearest showcase of his style.
  • Watch Ren Faire as a weekend binge before seeing Primetime, to see how he builds drama out of real people.
  • If you see You Can See Everything, pair it with HBO's The Inventor (2019) for the Theranos backstory.
Pay attention to
  • Spermworld deals frankly with sex and fertility, so it isn't one for family viewing.
  • Availability differs by country (HBO/Max, FX/Hulu or Disney+, theatrical), so check what's streaming where you are.
Links
  • Some Kind of Heaven (Dogwoof): https://releasing.dogwoof.com/some-kind-of-heaven
  • Lance Oppenheim filmography: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Oppenheim

Motion capture with three webcams and a printed checkerboard

FreeMoCap turns ordinary cameras into a markerless mocap rig, right down to the fingers.

verified★★★★★ Based on index.opensource (@index.opensource) · full analysis

Motion capture used to mean suits, markers and a studio. FreeMoCap, an open-source project led by Jon Matthis, starts from a few ordinary cameras instead. You calibrate them by waving a printed ChArUco checkerboard. An AI pose tracker finds the body, hands and face in each view, the 2D points are triangulated into 3D, and the result is cleaned of gaps and jitter.

What comes out is a full skeleton down to the fingers, plus a centre-of-mass trajectory that balance researchers use. An add-on sends the capture to Blender to drive a rigged character. The project launched with the pitch of mocap for about $100 in consumer webcams, and it's pip-installable.

For interactive and projection work, this is a cheap way to record real movement for animation, or to prototype body-driven visuals before you commit to expensive hardware.

Try this
  • Install it with pip install freemocap and record the bundled sample, or yourself, with two or three webcams.
  • Print the ChArUco board, calibrate, then capture a 30-second movement and export it to Blender.
  • Use the centre-of-mass data as a control signal for a visual, such as balance driving colour.
Pay attention to
  • The Blender export is still marked experimental.
  • The licence is AGPL-3.0, so check what that means before you build it into a commercial product.
  • "Research-grade" accuracy is the project's goal; it hasn't been independently benchmarked here.
Links
  • FreeMoCap: https://github.com/freemocap/freemocap
  • Documentation: https://freemocap.github.io/documentation
  • Blender: https://www.blender.org

Eating in Lucca without getting fleeced

Cecina, castagnaccio and a steam-oven focaccia: a short list of places that feed locals, not tour groups.

verified★★★★☆ Based on Alberto e Valerio | Slow Travel & Luoghi Insoliti 🧳 (@gliesploracose) · full analysis

Lucca is easy to love and easy to overpay in. The slow-travel duo Gli Esploracose put together a short, walkable list of places where locals actually eat, and the fact-check backs up the classics.

Start at Da Felice, a pizzeria that has been running for more than a century and is known for cecina, a thin chickpea-flour flatbread, and castagnaccio, a chestnut-flour cake. The historic Forno Amedeo Giusti steam-oven bakery is famous for its focaccia. Forno Casali adds pizzette and mortadella sandwiches. For a sit-down meal, Trattoria da Giulio has been open since 1945. The list ends with something more experimental at Pan di Strada, then gelato or granita at Gelateria Ele.

What ties it together is ordering what Lucca is known for (chickpeas, chestnuts, steam-baked dough) instead of a generic tourist menu.

Try this
  • Build a walking lunch: cecina at Da Felice, then focaccia at Giusti, then gelato at Ele.
  • Try castagnaccio if you never have. It's a seasonal, chestnut-flour taste of Tuscany.
  • Save the list to a map before you go, so you aren't searching on the street.
Pay attention to
  • Most of these are small shops with limited seating and their own opening hours, so check before you go.
  • The opening of the reel flashes "spoiler: trappola" (spoiler: trap) without explaining which place it means.
Links
  • Gambero Rosso, where to eat in Lucca: https://www.gamberorosso.it/notizie/dove-mangiare-lucca-lucca-comics-games

Comparing ETFs by cost, in one free tool

Choose a region and accumulating or distributing, and the cheapest funds rise to the top.

verified★★★★☆ Based on Dan Malone | Irish Investing Expert (@danmalonemoney) · full analysis

The hard part of index investing isn't picking an index. It's choosing among the dozens of near-identical funds that track it. The free ETF Comparison Tool on honest.ie does that sorting for you. Choose a region and whether you want an accumulating or a distributing fund, and it lists the indexes with their five-year returns and the matching ETFs ranked by total expense ratio (TER), with fact sheets and a side-by-side comparison.

It's built for Irish investors, but many of the funds it lists are the same UCITS ETFs sold across Europe, so it's also a quick way to get a feel for the cost differences between funds that track the same index. A "learn more" link shows which platforms sell each fund.

This is information, not advice: the tool shows costs and past returns, and it can't tell you what fits your situation.

Try this
  • Pick one index you already know, such as MSCI World, and see how far apart the cheapest and the most expensive trackers are on TER.
  • Open the fact sheet of a fund you own and check its TER and domicile against the tool.
  • Use the side-by-side view to compare an accumulating and a distributing version of the same fund.
Pay attention to
  • Tax treatment depends on where you live. Irish investors face exit tax and deemed disposal, and other countries have different rules.
  • Check fees and returns against each fund's KID or the issuer's own site before you act.
  • Past five-year returns don't predict the future.
Links
  • honest.ie ETF Comparison Tool: https://honest.ie/investing/etf/etf-comparison-tool/

Luisanna's secret for crispy potatoes is a teaspoon of baking soda

A quick alkaline blanch roughens the surface, and the rough surface becomes the crust.

verified★★★★★ Based on Instagram · full analysis

Tuscan cook Luisanna Messeri's trick for potatoes that are crisp outside and soft inside fits in a teaspoon. She blanches peeled wedges briefly in boiling water with a little baking soda, drains and dries them, fries them until golden, and salts them only at the end, with rosemary.

The science holds up. Alkaline water breaks down pectin on the potato's surface, which leaves a rough, starchy layer. That layer browns and crisps far better than a smooth cut surface. Salting at the end matters too: salt draws out moisture, and moisture is what stops things getting crisp.

The same principle works for oven-roasted potatoes. Sources suggest roughly a quarter to half a teaspoon of baking soda per litre of water and a few minutes of blanching.

Try this
  • Do a side-by-side test: half the batch blanched with baking soda, half without.
  • Shake the drained potatoes in the pot to scuff the surface even more before frying or roasting.
  • Dry them thoroughly on a cloth. Wet potatoes won't crisp.
Pay attention to
  • Too much baking soda tastes soapy. Stay around a teaspoon for a big pot.
  • Blanch briefly: overcooked wedges fall apart in the oil.
Links
  • Why it works (Italian): https://www.my-personaltrainer.it/alimentazione/come-avere-patate-arrosto-croccanti-fuori-e-morbide-dentro-segreto-chef-spiegato-dalla-scienza.html

Hand, face and pose tracking in TouchDesigner with one download

Torin Blankensmith's MediaPipe plugin comes as a single file, with nothing else to install.

verified★★★★★ Based on william (@wxll.hx) · full analysis

Body tracking in TouchDesigner used to mean installing Python packages and dealing with version conflicts. Torin Blankensmith's MediaPipe TouchDesigner plugin avoids all that. Download the latest release zip from GitHub (not the source code), open the included .toe file and wait a moment while the models load. You then have face, hand, pose and object tracking running inside TouchDesigner.

From there it's normal TouchDesigner work. Delete the trackers you don't need, take an output CHOP, put a Null after it and connect, for example, the hand landmarks to whatever you're driving. William's walkthrough shows the whole setup in seconds. Derivative's community tutorial covers the GPU-accelerated features in more depth.

For installations and projection mapping, this is one of the fastest ways to go from a webcam to a body-reactive visual.

Try this
  • Download the release, open the .toe and connect one hand landmark to a Transform TOP.
  • Combine it with a slit-scan or feedback effect so the effect follows the hand.
  • Turn off every tracker you don't use. It saves a lot of performance.
Pay attention to
  • Use the release zip, not "Source code"; the source download won't run as is.

macOS Tahoe added a small feature that's easy to miss: Shortcuts automations can now run when files are added to a folder. @octaflowtech uses it to keep the Downloads folder empty. Each time something lands there, the automation checks the file type. iPhone HEIC photos are converted to JPEG, resized so they're easy to email, and moved to Pictures. PDFs are renamed "Scan" plus today's date and moved to Documents.

The setup is: Shortcuts → Automation → Folder, choose Downloads, tick "Added" and set it to "Run Immediately". Then build a "Repeat with each" loop with an "If" for each file type. Every action it uses (Convert Image, Resize Image, Rename File, Move File) is a standard Shortcuts block.

It's a small change, and you stop thinking about the folder once it's set up.

Try this
  • Start with one rule, such as PDFs to Documents, and use it for a week before you add more.

  • Folder automations need macOS Tahoe (26) or later.

How to Hold a Cockroach, and why curiosity might be the cure

Matthew Maxwell's illustrated book argues that a lot of adult stress comes from forgetting how to try things like a child.

verified★★☆☆☆ Based on Bailey (@bailey.schildbach) · full analysis

Some books get passed hand to hand. Bailey's version is a selfie video in a parked car, recommending How to Hold a Cockroach: A Book for Those Who Are Free and Don't Know It, by writer, coach and meditation teacher Matthew Maxwell. It was first self-published and is now being reissued by Penguin.

The framing story is small. A boy is startled when a cockroach interrupts his dinner, and he starts to wonder how different the two of them really are. From there, the book works through themes like love, the past, the future, family and death. It asks which of our beliefs are really ours and which ones we picked up along the way.

The chapter Bailey describes will be familiar to many readers. A school assignment the author was proud of comes back with a harsh grade, and from then on, trying new things is shadowed by the fear of doing them wrong. The book's suggestion is to recover the curiosity you had as a child, when you tried things just to see what happened.

Her claim that this solves "99% of our problems" is enthusiasm, not a finding. As a gentle, illustrated nudge to loosen up, though, the book is real and easy to start.

Try this
  • Read or listen to one chapter a day instead of bingeing it, and note one belief it makes you question.
  • Pick something you stopped doing because you weren't 'good at it' and try it again for 20 minutes, just to see what happens.
  • Pass it to someone who's a perfectionist.
Pay attention to
  • It's a reflective self-help book, not therapy. If perfectionism or anxiety feels heavy, talk to a professional.
  • Editions and dates vary between the original self-published version and the new Penguin reissue.
Links
  • How to Hold a Cockroach (Penguin): https://www.penguin.com.au/books/how-to-hold-a-cockroach-9781807849481

One move, no equipment: the timed burpee circuit

Squat, push-up, mountain climber, hop back. Set a timer and you have a workout.

verified★★★☆☆ Based on Jason H. | Strength & Longevity Coach (@jasonstrongbeyond50) · full analysis

Jason H.'s "prison-style" workout is one compound move done as many times as you can in a set time. From standing, squat down, do a push-up, add a mountain climber, hop your feet back under you and stand up. Set a timer for one to five minutes depending on your fitness, rest a minute, and repeat for three to five rounds.

It's essentially a burpee variant used as high-intensity interval training, and research on bodyweight circuits like this one shows they reach genuinely high-intensity effort. Its main appeal is that you need almost nothing: no equipment, about two square metres of floor, and fifteen minutes.

To make it easier, do the push-up from your knees. To make it harder, lengthen the timer before you add more rounds.

Try this
  • Start with 3 rounds of 1 minute and count your reps, so you have a baseline to beat next week.
  • Do the push-up from your knees until your form holds for the whole timer.
  • Use it as a 15-minute workout on days when you can't get to a gym.
Pay attention to
  • Hopping and push-ups load your wrists, shoulders and knees. Stop if something hurts, and check with a professional if you have an injury.
  • Keep your form clean. Speed comes after.

Learn electronics in a week: a five-step starter plan

Start with an Arduino Uno, four components and a cheap multimeter, and leave the Raspberry Pi for later.

verified★★★★☆ Based on Armas Zarra (@armas.4am) · full analysis

Armas Zarra's beginner roadmap stands out because of what it leaves out. Start with an Arduino Uno, not a Wi-Fi board, so you learn power and reading data before networking. Wire one simple sensor to an analog pin and measure something real. Learn four components properly: the resistor, the capacitor, the diode and the transistor.

Then learn a handful of schematic symbols and the few sections of a datasheet that matter, such as pinout, absolute maximum ratings and typical application. Buy a cheap multimeter and debug by predicting a voltage before you measure it. Only after that should you move on to an ESP32 or a Raspberry Pi.

The fact-check agrees with the order: guides commonly recommend learning on the Uno and moving to the ESP32 later.

Try this
  • Get an Uno (or a clone) and a sensor kit, and read a potentiometer on an analog pin on day one.
  • Before every measurement, write down the voltage you expect, then measure it.
  • Read one real datasheet, such as an LED's or a transistor's, all the way through.
Pay attention to
  • The capacitor-as-tiny-battery analogy is a simplification. Capacitors discharge very differently from batteries.
  • Mains electricity is a different world. Stay with low-voltage DC while you're learning.

The vintage-shop way to cuff straight-leg jeans

Fold in, fold out, fold again. A clean roll that stays put.

verified★★★☆☆ Based on 古着屋PENNY CHIBA 柏店 (@penny_usedclothing) · full analysis

A Japanese used-clothing shop, PENNY CHIBA in Kashiwa, shows a hem roll that looks neater than a plain double cuff. Instead of folding the hem outward straight away, first fold it inward. Then fold it back up the other way, pulling it upward, fold that section once more, and finish with a small turned-up cuff.

The inner fold gives the cuff some structure, so it holds its shape and doesn't slide down. It works best on straight-leg jeans with a long inseam, where a plain cuff usually ends up bulky.

It costs nothing and takes thirty seconds, and it makes long jeans fit without a trip to the tailor.

Try this
  • Try it on your longest pair of straight-leg jeans and compare it with your usual cuff.
  • Do it in front of a mirror the first time. The direction of each fold matters.
Pay attention to
  • It's designed for straight legs. On skinny or tapered jeans it can look bunched.

The Tokyo record shop that ran on Bristol time

How Naoki Iijima's Disc Shop Zero turned a side-street shop into Japan's line to Bristol bass music.

verified★★★☆☆ Based on Noods Radio (@noodsradio) · full analysis

Before algorithms chose your next track, a scene travelled through people. Bristol station Noods Radio tells the story of one of them: Naoki Iijima, known as E-Jima, who opened Disc Shop Zero in Tokyo in 1993 and spent nearly three decades championing music from a city 6,000 miles away.

The shop first stocked the trip-hop that put Bristol on the map, Massive Attack, Tricky and Portishead. It moved with the city through dubstep, grime and drum and bass. Iijima didn't just sell records. He wrote about them, recommended them by hand and turned the shop into a meeting point for young Tokyo DJs. According to the film, that grew into an event series and label called BS0, after a made-up Bristol postcode, which brought UK producers over to play.

Resident Advisor confirms the outline: the 1993 opening, the Bristol focus and Iijima's death in February 2020. After he died, Bristol artists put together a fundraising compilation for his family. A few smaller details in the reel, like his first trip in 1994 and the honeymoon, are lovely but unconfirmed.

The lesson for anyone running a niche: obsession plus curation builds a bridge that outlives the shop.

Try this
  • Read Resident Advisor's piece on Iijima, then dig into the Bristol artists the film names: Rob Smith, Kahn, Neek and Young Echo.
  • Build a 'Bristol to Tokyo' playlist that runs from Massive Attack and Portishead to Bristol dubstep, in the order the shop sold them.
  • Find the record shop in your own city that champions one scene, and ask the owner what to listen to.
Pay attention to
  • Sources disagree on the shop's location (Ekoda or Shimokitazawa), and one guide says it has since closed, so don't plan a visit without checking.
  • The BS0 label details, the 1994 trip and the honeymoon come from the reel and weren't independently confirmed.
Links
  • Resident Advisor on Naoki Iijima: https://www.residentadvisor.net/news/71952
  • DJ Mag on the Disc Shop Zero fundraiser: https://djmag.com/news/denham-audio-mantra-sully-more-contribute-fundraising-compilation-tokyo%E2%80%99s-disc-shop-zero

It runs from Santa Fiora on Monte Amiata through the Vitozza cave village near Sorano and Niki de Saint Phalle's Tarot Garden, to the Etruscan site of Populonia on the coast.

mixed★★★☆☆ Polyrhythm drum machine in TouchDesigner Ilgın İçözü (@ilginicozu)
touchdesignermixed→ triage-touchdesigner
What it shows: A speed tutorial ("How to create a polyrhythm in TouchDesigner using MOPs, under 60 seconds") that builds a small drum machine from operators in a "MOP" tab of TouchDesigner's OP Create dialog. A clock feeds a clock divider whose outputs trigger a kick and a snare/hi-hat generator, mixed down to Audio Out, over a white point-cloud visual.

Key points:
- Clock → Clock Divider. The 1/3 output triggers the kick (pitch amount 2.81, pitch decay 0.05).
- Snare & Hihat: tune 160, tone/noise mix 0.2, noise decay 0.05, drive 2.3. Divider 1/8 triggers the snare and 1/6 the hi-hat.
- Kick and snare/hi-hat go into a 4-channel mixer, then Audio Out.
- Dividing one clock by 3, 6 and 8 gives the interlocking polyrhythm.

Links:
- TouchDesigner: https://derivative.ca
- TouchDesigner operator families (docs): https://docs.derivative.ca/Operator
- MOPs operator set: source not found (unverified)

Claims checked:
- "MOPs" is a TouchDesigner operator family — unclear: Derivative's docs list TOPs, CHOPs, POPs, MATs, DATs, SOPs and COMPs, not MOPs, so it's likely a third-party or custom palette https://docs.derivative.ca/Operator
- A polyrhythm can be built by dividing one clock and triggering drum voices — confirmed as shown on screen. This is a standard technique, and the frames show the full network and parameters.

Verdict: mixed — the patch is shown step by step, but the "MOPs" operators aren't standard TouchDesigner and I couldn't find where to get them.

verified★★★★☆ Slit-scan effect in 3 nodes william (@wxll.hx)
touchdesignerverified→ triage-touchdesigner
What it shows: William (@wxll.hx) builds a slit-scan / time-displacement effect in TouchDesigner with three nodes in 15 seconds. A video or webcam feeds a Texture 3D TOP (cache size 80), which feeds a Time Machine TOP with black offset -80.

Key points:
- Add a video or webcam input (Movie File In / Video Device In TOP)
- Add a Texture 3D TOP and set cache size to 80
- Add a Time Machine TOP and set black offset to -80
- Connect the video to the Time Machine as well, so it's used as the time map
- Result: a smeared, time-warped image

verified★★★☆☆ How YOLO object detection works index.opensource (@index.opensource)
aiverified→ triage-ai
What it shows: index.opensource explains how Ultralytics YOLO (version YOLO26) detects objects, using pigeon footage, the original arXiv paper and the Ultralytics source code. It covers the 640 px input, three detection grids, box regression as distances to the four edges, NMS filtering versus the new NMS-free head, and the AGPL-3.0 license.

Key points:
- YOLO = You Only Look Once, introduced by Joseph Redmon et al. in 2015
- Frames are resized to 640 px and predictions are made on three grids (P3–P5)
- Each cell predicts box distances to four edges plus scores for 80 COCO classes
- Classic head needs NMS to remove duplicate boxes; YOLO26 adds an NMS-free one-to-one head
- Code and models are AGPL-3.0; commercial closed use needs an Ultralytics Enterprise license

Links:
- Ultralytics (GitHub): https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics
- Ultralytics YOLO26 docs: https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo26/
- YOLO paper (arXiv 1506.02640): https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02640

Claims checked:
- YOLO was introduced by Joseph Redmon in 2015 — confirmed: arXiv "You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection" (submitted June 2015) https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02640
- YOLO26 has an NMS-free (one-to-one) head, with an NMS head as alternative — confirmed: Ultralytics YOLO26 docs https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo26/
- Code and models are AGPL-3.0, with an Enterprise license to avoid source sharing — confirmed: Ultralytics YOLO26 docs https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo26/
- Default input size 640, 80 classes, 0.25 confidence threshold — confirmed: Ultralytics default.yaml shown on screen https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics

Verdict: verified — a careful, source-backed explainer.

- It runs on Linux/WSL, Windows and macOS, so you don't need a Mac.
- Login choice: an API key (needs the paid Apple Developer Program) or a password (any Apple ID, through private APIs). The tool itself advises using a secondary Apple ID for password mode.

What it shows: An explainer from @index.opensource (English with Korean subtitles) on FreeMoCap, an open-source markerless motion-capture system by Jon Matthis and the FreeMoCap Foundation. A classroom sample filmed with three ordinary cameras becomes a 3D skeleton (body, hands, face, centre of mass), which then drives an animated skeleton character in Blender.

Key points:
- Markerless motion capture from several ordinary cameras: no suits or markers needed
- Pipeline: calibrate cameras with a printed (ChArUco) checkerboard → an AI pose tracker finds body, hands and face in each view → triangulate 2D points into 3D → fill gaps and smooth jitter
- Outputs a full skeleton down to the fingers, plus a body centre-of-mass trajectory (used in balance research)
- Exports to Blender to drive a rigged character
- Software is AGPL-licensed; the sample recording is CC BY 4.0

- Whisper can transcribe locally — confirmed: open-source model that runs on-device; GitHub https://github.com/openai/whisper

Verdict: verified — a sound, accurate cost-saving approach: pre-process video locally and give Claude a summary plus a contact sheet instead of raw frames.

- A good reference for an image-to-sound sonification pipeline (TD → Pd, most likely via OSC)

mixed★★☆☆☆ Headache self-release routine West Texas Recovery Room (@westtexasrecoveryroom)
healthto checkhealthmixed→ triage-health
What it shows: A clinician from West Texas Recovery Room, in scrubs, demonstrates a self-administered "suboccipital release" routine for headaches and migraines. It covers gentle thumb strokes down the sternocleidomastoid (SCM) to the collarbone, pressure into the soft hollows at the base of the skull, 30-second neck stretches, and a final relaxed head cradle.

Key points:
- Step 1: thumb glides from behind the ear down the SCM to the clavicle, both sides, gently
- Step 2: thumbs (or index fingers) into the two hollows under the back of the skull, press in and stroke downward while looking down; then repeat slightly further out
- Step 3: hands clasped behind the back, shoulders dropped, side-bend and chin-down stretches held 30 s each, both sides
- Step 4: cradle the skull in your hands and let the neck relax with small movements
- Aimed at headache/migraine relief through neck soft-tissue release

Links:
- West Texas Recovery Room (creator's clinic; Instagram @westtexasrecoveryroom): https://www.instagram.com/westtexasrecoveryroom/ (unverified)

Claims checked:
- Suboccipital/neck soft-tissue work can relieve headaches — confirmed for tension-type headache (low-to-moderate evidence): soft-tissue manual therapy reduces pain intensity and frequency vs. no treatment, though the trials use therapist-applied techniques, not self-massage; "Manual therapy in adults with tension-type headache: A systematic review" (Neurología 2021) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34537167/
- Suboccipital (and SCM) trigger points are linked to headache — confirmed: active suboccipital trigger points were found in 65% of chronic tension-type headache patients and tracked with headache intensity; Fernández-de-las-Peñas et al. 2006, summarised at Chiro.org https://chiro.org/Headache/Trigger_Points_in_the_Suboccipital_Muscles.shtml
- It helps migraines — unclear: the evidence is mainly for tension-type and cervicogenic headache, not migraine
- The skull has "two little holes called occipitals" you press into — contradicted (terminology): the hollows you feel are the soft-tissue suboccipital region below the occipital bone, not holes in the skull; Kenhub, "Suboccipital muscles" https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/suboccipital-muscles

Verdict: mixed — a reasonable, low-risk self-care routine for tension-type headaches, but the migraine claim is weakly supported and the anatomy is described inaccurately.

verified★★★★☆ Italian inheritance tax: 3 legal tools Luca Terragnoli Consulente Patrimoniale (@lucaterragnoli_consulente)
financeto checkhacksverified→ triage-finance
What it shows: An Italian wealth consultant (Luca Terragnoli) gives "3 trucchi" for passing assets to your children in Italy while paying little or no inheritance/gift tax, calling them three perfectly legal tools people ignore. (The auto-transcript was garbled; the content comes from the on-screen Italian subtitles.)

Key points:
- Billions are transferred by inheritance in Italy each year, and thousands of families pay taxes they could legally avoid
- 1. Donazione (lifetime gift): the law lets you gift up to a threshold per child tax-free, which can zero out the tax if done correctly
- 2. Life insurance policy with designated beneficiaries: the payout stays outside the estate and isn't subject to inheritance tax, as long as it doesn't infringe the forced-heirship shares
- 3. Gift the bare ownership (nuda proprietà) while keeping the usufruct: suited to property or company shares; children pay no tax and you keep full use of the asset for life
- Ends with an offer to tell you which solution fits your case

Links:
- none mentioned

Claims checked:
- Gifts/inheritance to children are tax-free up to €1,000,000 per beneficiary, with 4% above that — confirmed: QuiFinanza, "Imposta sulle donazioni e calcolo delle franchigie" https://quifinanza.it/fisco-tasse/imposta-donazioni-calcolo-franchigie-aliquote/1010806/
- Earlier gifts count toward the franchigia — confirmed (a nuance the reel skips): Agenzia delle Entrate Risposta n. 571/2021 https://www.studiocerbone.com/?p=452811
- Life policy proceeds paid to named beneficiaries fall outside the inheritance declaration/tax — confirmed: Moneyfarm, "Come evitare la tassa sulla successione" https://blog.moneyfarm.com/it/proteggi-il-tuo-capitale/come-evitare-la-tassa-sulla-successione/
- Gifting bare ownership while keeping usufruct is a legal transfer tool — confirmed in principle (standard Italian practice); the tax savings depend on valuation and the €1M franchigia, which the reel doesn't spell out. Fiscomania, "Passaggio beni successione eredità" https://fiscomania.com/passaggio-beni-successione-eredita/

Verdict: verified — the three tools are real and legal; the "zero tax" framing only holds within the €1M per-child franchigia and with proper advice.

verified★★★☆☆ 5 types of income ETFs Matteo Tonarelli (@apprendista_investitore)
financeto checkfinanceverified→ triage-finance
What it shows: Matteo Tonarelli (Apprendista Investitore), in Italian, explains "ETF che ti pagano uno stipendio": 5 types of income ETFs, with an example fund for each and its trade-offs, plus an Italian tax note. (The auto-transcript was garbled; the content comes from the on-screen captions and graphics.)

Key points:
- 1. High-dividend equity, e.g. Vanguard FTSE All-World High Dividend Yield (~2,000 companies), paying monthly or quarterly
- 2. Covered call: dividends plus option premiums, e.g. JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income; high payouts (monthly, some even weekly) but capped growth
- 3. Bond ETFs, e.g. iShares Italy Govt Bond: more stable, less growth; for Italians, government bonds are taxed at 12.5% instead of 26%
- 4. Money-market ETFs, e.g. Xtrackers II EUR Overnight Rate Swap: like a deposit account, low volatility and high liquidity, but accumulating, so it pays no dividend and you "earn" by selling
- 5. REIT ETFs, e.g. iShares Developed Markets Property Yield: property income without tenants, usually monthly or quarterly payouts

verified★★★★☆ texture-synthesis: grow textures from a sample index.opensource (@index.opensource)
opensourceto checkopensourceverified→ triage-opensource
What it shows: An index.opensource explainer of Embark Studios' texture-synthesis, a Rust library that grows a new, non-repeating image from one small example photo. It explains the pixel-by-pixel algorithm with visual debug maps, then shows guided synthesis, hole filling (inpainting), seamless tiling and the README's stated weakness with regular patterns.

Key points:
- Example-based (non-parametric) texture synthesis: fills the canvas pixel by pixel, matching neighbourhoods in the source image.
- Uses 50 neighbouring pixels by default (--k-neighs), so whole patches get copied together.
- Supports guide maps, inpainting with a mask and seamless tiling.
- Weak spot: regular textures like bricks (visible seams).
- Dual-licensed MIT / Apache-2.0; the repo was archived in Oct 2023 (read-only, no longer maintained).

- It's a loan, not a gift, and requires a bank-backed LBO.

- "There are no buyers" / "France will give you €5M" — contradicted: about 130,000 transfers are still expected by 2030, and the money is a loan alongside bank debt; Les 370 000 transmissions… (Le Journal des Entreprises) https://www.lejournaldesentreprises.com/article/les-370-000-transmissions-dentreprises-attendues-en-cinq-ans-vont-devoir-saffranchir-de-nombreux-2131742

Verdict: mixed — The figures and loan terms are accurate, but the "France will give you €5M / zero buyers" framing is a sales hook.
